s1.syndrome_frame: intermittent colicky abdominal pain with rectal bleeding and mucopurulent discharge
salient_findings: intermittent colicky pain in the left iliac fossa
blood-mixed stool
large amounts of mucopurulent discharge per rectum
exophytic mass at the descending–sigmoid junction
intussusception of the descending colon into the sigmoid colon
key_facts: no family history of gastrointestinal disease
unremarkable abdominal and digital rectal examinations
colonoscopy revealed a 5 × 5 cm exophytic mass
contrast-enhanced CT showed a well-defined hypodense lesion

raw.syndrome_frame: intermittent colicky abdominal pain with rectal bleeding and mucopurulent discharge
salient_findings: intermittent colicky pain in the left iliac fossa
blood-mixed stool
large amounts of mucopurulent discharge per rectum
exophytic mass at the descending–sigmoid junction
intussusception of the descending colon into the sigmoid colon
key_facts: no family history of gastrointestinal disease

differentials: Inflammatory myofibroblastic tumor of the colon
per_call: Inflammatory myofibroblastic tumor of the colon

shortlist.label: Sigmoid colon cancer
shortlist.why_kept: exophytic mass at the descending–sigmoid junction with surface exudates and erosions

shortlist.label: Intussusception of the colon
shortlist.why_kept: invagination of the descending colon into the sigmoid colon consistent with intussusception

shortlist.label: Colonic polyp
shortlist.why_kept: colonoscopy revealed a 5 × 5 cm exophytic mass, possible polypoid lesion

shortlist.label: Diverticulitis
shortlist.why_kept: intermittent colicky abdominal pain with rectal bleeding and mucopurulent discharge, possible diverticular disease

shortlist.label: Gastrointestinal stromal tumor
shortlist.why_kept: exophytic mass with surface exudates and erosions, possible gastrointestinal stromal tumor

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings, including the invagination of the descending colon into the sigmoid colon and a well-defined hypodense lesion, are consistent with intussusception of the colon, which is further supported by the presence of an exophytic mass causing partial obstruction.

rejected.label: Sigmoid colon cancer
rejected.why: Normal carcinoembryonic antigen level and the specific imaging features suggesting intussusception make cancer less likely as the primary diagnosis.

rejected.label: Colonic polyp
rejected.why: The size of the exophytic mass and the presence of intussusception are not typical for a simple polyp.

rejected.label: Diverticulitis
rejected.why: The absence of significant abdominal tenderness, fever, or elevated inflammatory markers makes diverticulitis less likely.

rejected.label: Gastrointestinal stromal tumor
rejected.why: While possible, the specific findings of intussusception and the characteristics of the mass are more suggestive of intussusception due to another cause rather than a primary tumor like GIST.
